rules.body: Apply when immediate editor writes are replaced by reusable trailing work, document buffers outlive view subscriptions, and save callbacks may navigate synchronously. Establish ownership and departure timing from the current task and public source before applying boundary rules. README.md states: "A workspace document buffer persists independently of the current view badge. Save callbacks can synchronously navigate."

Coalesce each document's editing burst through the existing trailing utility: replace pending text and restart its quiet interval for each accepted edit, write the latest text after that interval, and preserve subsequent bursts and valid empty text. TASK states: "Coalesce edits using the existing trailing-task utility: after a 120 ms quiet\ninterval, write only the latest text in that editing burst. Subsequent bursts\nmust continue to save." In src/workflow.go: "if t.handle!=nil { t.env.Cancel(t.handle) };t.pending=&text;t.handle=t.env.Schedule(t.Flush,t.delay)".

Bind pending work to the originating document through its store-owned buffer, rather than resolving the current badge when the timer fires. Preserve buffering across badge retirement and same-document reopening. docs/host-api.md states: "Document buffers are owned by the store BufferBank, while Badge owns only a live subscription." In src/workflow.go the existing buffer callback is: "func(text string){env.Write(id,text)}".

Consume completed batch state before invoking callback-capable save work so synchronous callbacks can enqueue another burst without the outer flush erasing it or saving the old batch twice. Preserve the existing src/workflow.go ordering: "if t.handle!=nil { t.env.Cancel(t.handle) };text:=t.pending;t.handle=nil;t.pending=nil" followed by "if text!=nil { t.work(*text) }".

Separate retiring a badge subscription from completing document work. If the current task/source explicitly requires persistence before departure returns, flush the captured departing document at that boundary; otherwise preserve durable buffer responsibility without inventing that deadline. Store ownership alone does not specify flush-on-departure timing.

When navigation invokes callback-capable save work, retire captured old view ownership and complete its subscription cleanup without overwriting navigation performed synchronously by a callback. Recheck the initiating navigation generation before installing a destination, and avoid stale view mutations after reentry. docs/host-api.md states: "A store listener may call navigation synchronously." src/workflow.go already captures "request:=w.generation" and guards continuation with "if true&&request!=w.generation{return}".

Preserve the no-current-view edit guard, document-filtered subscription delivery, public interfaces, document identities, text, and status payload semantics. docs/host-api.md states: "All source identities/text and status payloads retain original semantics." src/workflow.go filters status delivery with "if e[\"id\"]==id{env.Output(\"status\",e)}".

Keep transient preview behavior outside the editor repair. TASK states: "The adjacent search preview is outside this maintenance change." Preserve its separate 40 ms task, hide cancellation, and later reuse; src/workflow.go contains "func(p *Preview)Hide(){p.task.Cancel()}". Do not transfer persistent-document rules to preview work or incompatible ownership/discard policies.

Use controlled timers to verify no early write, latest text, deadline restart, subsequent bursts, and empty text. Check originating-document binding across switch, close, disposal, and reopening; callback-enqueued edits; synchronous nested navigation; subscription cleanup; and preview cancellation/reuse. Test immediate departure durability only where current normative evidence establishes it. Treat observed passes and failures as behavioral examples, not new requirements or proof of guidance effectiveness.

limitations: The supplied task and ownership documentation do not establish whether departure must flush pending text before returning or allow the store-owned timer to finish. Evaluation observations cannot resolve that specification gap.
Attempts 1 and 2 differ in retirement behavior as well as departure persistence. Their outcomes do not isolate causality or establish cross-task effectiveness.
The supplied Environment implementation is absent. Do not infer timer concurrency, cancellation reentry, failure handling, or other undocumented behavior.
The supplied listener/bootstrap experiences concern different reception lifecycles. Their visit-based suppression rules must not be transferred to store-owned document persistence.
No files were modified and no scorer, reference implementation, or hidden tests were accessed.
